_meta.purpose: Draft source registry for Niswah's implemented fiqh rules and the madhhab reference works/institutions that could ground them. Built during the Source Governance, Madhhab Authority, Jurisdiction Sources, and Fiqh Advisor Grounding wave (2026-09-09).
_meta.warning: THIS IS AN ENGINEERING-PRODUCED DRAFT, NOT A SCHOLARLY VERIFICATION. It was compiled by an AI assistant (Claude, via Claude Code) from general Islamic-studies knowledge, not from direct inspection of a primary text or confirmation by a qualified Islamic scholar. Reference-work titles/authors named below are genuine, well-known works standardly associated with each madhhab (the kind of attribution found in any comparative-fiqh textbook) -- but NO specific chapter/page/section number is asserted for any of them, because that could not be verified against a specific edition this session and a wrong page citation would misrepresent a real book. Every rule below is 'source_confidence: AI_RECALLED_UNVERIFIED' and 'reviewer_status: NOT_REVIEWED' until a qualified Islamic scholar with direct access to these texts confirms or corrects the mapping.
_meta.do_not: Do not present any entry in this file as a citable, page-accurate religious source. Do not mark reviewer_status as APPROVED without a named qualified reviewer. Do not deploy this registry as the sole grounding basis for a live ruling without scholar sign-off.

hanafi.title: Al-Hidayah fi Sharh Bidayat al-Mubtadi
hanafi.author: Burhan al-Din al-Marghinani (d. 593 AH / 1197 CE)
hanafi.reference_section: NOT_LOCATED_THIS_PASS — Kitab al-Taharah (Book of Purity) is the standard section for hayd/haid rulings in this genre of text; exact chapter/page not verified this pass

hanafi.title: Radd al-Muhtar ala al-Durr al-Mukhtar (Hashiyat Ibn Abidin)
hanafi.author: Ibn Abidin (Muhammad Amin ibn Abidin, d. 1252 AH / 1836 CE)
hanafi.type: canonical late-Hanafi commentary, widely treated as an authoritative modern reference within the school

hanafi.title: Al-Fatawa al-Hindiyyah (al-Fatawa al-Alamgiriyyah)
hanafi.author: Compiled by a board of Hanafi scholars under Mughal patronage (17th century CE)

maliki.title: Al-Mudawwana al-Kubra
maliki.author: Sahnun ibn Sa'id al-Tanukhi (transmitting Imam Malik's students, d. 240 AH / 854 CE)

maliki.title: Mukhtasar Khalil (Mukhtasar al-Allamah Khalil)
maliki.author: Khalil ibn Ishaq al-Jundi (d. 776 AH / 1374 CE)
maliki.type: canonical, widely-taught Maliki summary text with extensive later commentary tradition

maliki.title: Al-Risala (Risalat Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani)
maliki.author: Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani (d. 386 AH / 996 CE)

shafii.title: Al-Umm
shafii.author: Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i (d. 204 AH / 820 CE)
shafii.type: foundational Shafi'i text, the school's eponymous founder's own compiled work

shafii.title: Minhaj al-Talibin
shafii.author: Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH / 1277 CE)
shafii.type: canonical, extremely widely-relied-upon later Shafi'i reference with a large commentary tradition

shafii.title: Al-Majmu Sharh al-Muhadhdhab
shafii.author: Yahya ibn Sharaf al-Nawawi (d. 676 AH / 1277 CE), completed after his death by later scholars
shafii.type: extensive canonical Shafi'i commentary, frequently cited on menstruation/purity rulings specifically

hanbali.title: Al-Mughni
hanbali.author: Ibn Qudamah al-Maqdisi (d. 620 AH / 1223 CE)
hanbali.type: canonical, comparative-fiqh-oriented Hanbali reference, widely cited across madhahib for its comparative structure

hanbali.title: Kashaf al-Qina an Matn al-Iqna
hanbali.author: Mansur ibn Yunus al-Buhuti (d. 1051 AH / 1641 CE)

hanbali.title: Zad al-Mustaqni fi Ikhtisar al-Muqni
hanbali.author: Musa al-Hajjawi (d. 968 AH / 1560 CE)
hanbali.type: widely-taught concise Hanbali primer, standard curriculum text in many contemporary Hanbali-tradition institutions (notably Saudi Arabia)
